features.context: Gender identity and expression can vary across generations.
Cultural norms, legal recognition of non-binary genders, and language differences affect how people respond.
The wording of the question (e.g., “sex” vs. “gender identity”) and available response options (e.g., male/female only vs. inclusive options) heavily influence answers.
Binary (male/female) → Predicts high conformity to binary choices; inclusive options allow for greater diversity in responses.
“What is your biological sex?” → Likely leads to binary answers; “What is your gender identity?” → Opens up responses based on self-identification.
Some cultures recognize third genders; others enforce strict binary norms.
